## Goal
This page outlines the data management choices made within the MOMENTUM 3.0 project. Two main goals are addressed. The first goal is to have an **overall MOMENTUM data collection** where all data generated within the MOMENTUM 3.0 project is stored in a **sustainable and FAIR**, overseen by Utrecht University (UU). The idea is that all partners of MOMENTUM 3.0 have access to all data generated within the current project (and, where possible, previous projects). The second goal is to have **all the relevant data** from MOMENTUM 3.0 in the **eNanomapper (ENM) database**, so this data can be reused by researchers and serve as input for risk assessments now and in the future. 

## Data Strategy

### 1. MOMENTUM data collection
The Partner Assembly (PA) of MOMENTUM 3.0 agreed that all data that is collected in the MOMENTUM 3.0 project should be stored at one location and remains available to the consortium after the project ends. For this, YODA has been selected as the data repository in MOMENTUM 3.0. Storing all MOMENTUM 3.0 data centrally on YODA is compulsory for partners in the MOMENTUM 3.0 project. 

For this, all data underlying publications must be uploaded in YODA. Additionally, unpublished data should, as much as possible, be uploaded to YODA whenever ready, or within 1 year after the end of the MOMENTUM 3.0 project. 
Data underlying publications need to be organized in simple folders with sufficient documentation to make sense of this data (include e.g. readme files) per publication. These bundles of data shall be published (and archived) in YODA, with closed/restricted/open access (with DOI if requested). A similar structuring of data should be used for non-published data, for instance grouping per MOMENTUM partner/data generator or per Work Package. 

### 2. eNanoMapper (ENM)
The Partner Assembly (PA) of MOMENTUM 3.0 decided that all tabular experimental data on particles (including -omics and exposure data) is filled into ENM templates for uploading into the ENM database. ENM provides an added layer of FAIRness and enables combining research output from different sources.

To get (experimental) data into ENM, researchers (or data generators) use the appropriate ENM template and upload these templates to YODA. Predefined templates are available in the Wizard on the website of ENM. The ENM Designer can be used to create custom-made templates to fit individual data needs. Experimental data in ENM templates should be uploaded to a dedicated YODA folder that will be regularly parsed into the ENM database.

### 3. Timeline
It is advised to start following this MOMENTUM 3.0 Data Strategy as early as possible in your research. If possible, use the ENM templates during your data collection. All your data underlaying a publication should be collected in a separate data package. Making this data package for each publication should be part of the researchers own data management. Each data generator can make their data available via YODA and in ENM as soon as the data is final. There is no need to wait until a paper is published. Data should be uploaded in YODA in data packages, including filled ENM templates, own Excel files and non-tabular data. If data of the MOMENTUM 3.0 project is published in a paper and the data is not yet available in YODA and/or ENM , make sure to have the data uploaded maximally 2 months after the publication. If a researcher foresees issues with this timeline, this should be discussed with their Work Package leader.

### 4. Other repositories
Every partner in MOMENTUM is free to use additional repositories to publish the data that is also uploaded in YODA, for example via a journal. Make sure to have a good registration of version control in case different copies of the data is published.

### 5. Uploading, DOI, and version control
The data should be organized into data packages containing tabular (experimental data in ENM Excel templates or own template) Data generators will get access to YODA to place their data in YODA. An overview of  data requirements is provided in the checklist (will follow). Data gets a DOI and, if applicable, data will be made available via open access. In case of restricted access, a data sharing protocol needs to be arranged by the data owner - there are usually institutional guidelines available to be consulted.

The data should be organized into data packages containing tabular (experimental data in ENM Excel templates or own template) and non-tabular data (images, PCR, literature review and modelling outputs, SOPs etc.) with proper documentation. All data can be uploaded whenever they are ready, waiting until the publication is online is not necessary.
Make sure to upload the latest version of data to YODA. When local changes are made to the data (e.g. on researcher’s own institutional drive), the version on YODA always needs to be updated.

### 6. Documentation and metadata
Systematically documented research data is the key to making the data publishable, discoverable, citable and reusable. Clear and detailed documentation improve the overall data quality, hence both (future) you and your peers benefit from it. It is vital to document both the study for which the data has been collected and the data itself. These two levels of documentation are called project-level documentation and data-level documentation.
Most data documentation is primarily readable for humans. Meanwhile, metadata is intended for machine-reading. This metadata or "data about data" are descriptors that facilitate cataloguing data and data discovery. When data is submitted to YODA, the archive generates machine-readable metadata. Machine-readable metadata help to explain the purpose, origin, time, location, creator(s), terms of use, and access conditions of research data.
Please refer to other extensive resources to learn more about data documentation and best practices (for example UU guidelines, CESSDA guidebook).

### 7. Accessibility 
The data in YODA can be published with open, restricted or closed access. The data owner determines the level of access. In all cases the data gets an identifier (DOI) assigned, which can be referenced in the published paper. In general, as long as openness is legally and ethically permissible, MOMENTUM 3.0 data should be made open access. However, in case of restricted access, an access protocol and data-sharing agreements need to be prepared to ensure that access to the data can be provided in a timely manner. These documents should be arranged and managed by the data owner.

### 8. Licensing
In YODA there are several licenses available (when you fill in the metadata). A data license agreement is a legal instrument that informs others what they can and cannot do with given research data (and any documentation, scripts and metadata that are published with the data). It is important to consider what kind of limitations are relevant.
The considerations below form the basis of the [Creative Common (CC)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/) licenses:
- Can copies be made or even distributed?
- Do others (and you) reusing the dataset need to acknowledge you as the author of the original dataset? (“Attribution”)
- Do others (and you) who reuse the dataset and/or make derivatives of the dataset need to share their work under a similar licence? (“Share-Alike”)
- Can others (and you) use your dataset commercially? (A restriction on commercial use is called “Non-Commercial”)
- Can others (and you) create a new work based on the dataset? (“Derivative”)

There are other considerations and licenses as well, however, CC licenses are commonly used. If you need help choosing a CC license, please check this and this resource.

#### Custom licenses
When dealing with personal data, confidential data or data protected by intellectual property rights, CC licences may not be appropriate. It is advised to use a custom licence in those cases.

In a custom licence you can determine precisely how your data may be used and what ought not to be done with the data (i.e. do not attempt to identify individuals). Drawing up a custom license agreement without prior experience can be difficult. If you need help with this, please contact your institute’s RDM support, privacy officer or legal office.

#### Implementing a custom license in YODA
When using a custom license, please make sure to upload the license agreement as a PDF file in YODA. In the metadata of the data package, please indicate that a custom license is used and refer to the uploaded license agreement.
When filling in the metadata, there are several licenses available in YODA, such as different types of Creative Commons licenses or an Open Data Commons license.
In case the listed licenses are not suitable for your data package, or if you publish your data package under Restricted or Closed Access, you should create a custom license instead. When Custom is chosen, a License.txt file must be uploaded into the main folder of the data package. The custom license must provide information about: 
- Access conditions: how can access can be requested? What does the requester need to do or deliver before gaining access? At the very least, provide a contact point in the data package description. 
- Usage conditions:
    - Permissions: who can reuse the data and for which purposes (research, education, commercial)?
    - Obligations: for example, are there requirements related to data security?
    - Prohibitions: for example, are there restrictions to sharing the data further?

### 9. Minimal requirements 
The minimum data to be reported are **all data underlying publications**. Preferably both raw and processed data should be uploaded to YODA and as much as possible made available also in ENM. The level of "rawness" is determined by the data owner, based on their expertise and understanding of the data. If providing raw data in ENM compatible format requires substantial effort and is deemed unfeasible within the given project timeline the data owner should contact the MOMENTUM coordinator. When no actual data can be made public either on YODA and/or ENM, at least basic metadata describing the research methodology should be provided.
Folder structure in YODA should be simple and generics. Folders will be structured per work package, with separate folders per publication, containing folders of ENM templates and all other formats (see image 1. below for inspiration). Please reach out if you need advice on how to organise data.

![](/images/simple_datapack.png "1. Simple folder structure for publications within work packages")

If restricted access is chosen under specific licenses when publishing, only metadata will be accessible.

The two **streams** of MOMENTUM data (ENM and YODA) can be linked on the [website of MOMENTUM](https://momentummicroplastics.nl/) or the MOMENTUM [community](https://zenodo.org/communities/momentum/records?q=&l=list&p=1&s=10&sort=newest) on ZENODO.

### 10. Route
Data generators will get access to YODA to place their data in YODA. An overview of  data requirements is provided in the checklist below. The data is placed in ENM templates for export to ENM. The ENM templates and other templates/formats will be stored in the YODA vault. Data gets a DOI and, if applicable, data will be made available via open access. In case of restricted access, a data sharing protocol needs to be arranged by the data owner - there are usually institutional guidelines available to be consulted.

The UU data steward is available to assist with the ENM templates and other steps.

### 11. Data checklist

| Type of data generated | Data storage |
| :---------- | :----------- |
| • Experimental, Tabular Data - xls, csv <br><br> e.g. Lab data (raw & processed)  | data into enanomapper (ENM) template <br><br> » store templates together with original data in YODA |
| • Experimental, Non-Tabular Data <br><br> e.g. Output of imaging techniques, PCR | store all formats in YODA |
| • Non-Experimental Data <br><br> e.g. Documentation, SOPs, literature reviews, modelling output	| store all formats in YODA|
|<strong>Openness</strong> <br><br> • Open <br><br> • Restricted - metadata is open |<strong>Required documents</strong> (in case of restricted access) <br><br> • protocol available for arranging data access <br><br> » e.g. contact person appointed, data-sharing agreements in place – usually institutional guidelines to be consulted|
